transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Markus (CT Head of Platform), Priya (CT ML), Jonah (CT Security), Ava (CT Product)

Summary / Topics (auto): quickstart credits, Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, required compliance (SOC2/KMS), latency SLO, pilot timeline, benchmark and next steps

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, I'm Samira, AE on Redwood inference — Diego and Lena from our solutions team are with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Markus: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat. We kicked this off because we need to pick a path for a pilot — ideally quick to integrate but with a clear path to VPC or on-prem later.
[00:18] Samira: Perfect. High level plan today: run through your use case, constraints, timeline, then walk through options — hosted API quickstart with credits, Dedicated reserved pool, or Private (VPC/on-prem). Then capture next steps. Does that work?
[00:27] Markus: Yep.
[00:29] Priya: Quick note, we have two goals: a prototype in 2-3 weeks to demo to product, and a production pilot in ~8 weeks if perf checks out. Latency target is sub-300ms p50 for single-turn routing responses, p95 under 600ms ideally. Cost is a big factor too.
[00:43] Diego: Okay that helps. Can you give a sense of expected QPS and prompt lengths?
[00:47] Priya: Baseline ~10 qps for the pilot, burst to 60 qps during peak. Prompts average 600 tokens including context, expecting mostly instruction-following model behavior with some short KV cache reuse.
[01:02] Lena: When you say KV cache, are you caching conversation state or route history?
[01:06] Priya: Route history and recent deliveries; small prefix reuse between calls, maybe 50-100 tokens repeated.
[01:12] Jonah: From security, we need encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, audit logs retained 1 year, and SSO via Okta. Also we may need to push for Private later because some customers require data residency and extra isolation.
[01:25] Samira: Totally reasonable. We support all of those across our modes: Hosted supports KMS and audit logs, Dedicated can be provisioned in isolated GPU pools and VPC peering, and Private gives you a customer-managed plane. SSO via SAML/Okta is supported.
[01:39] Jonah: On the hosted side — what about PII/PHI handling? We might have some rider notes with personal identifiers.
[01:46] Diego: Hosted by default processes data in our tenancy; we have SOC2 and can offer higher retention controls via add-ons. For regulated workloads we usually recommend Dedicated or Private, but many customers do prototypes on hosted first using obfuscation or tokenization.
[02:02] Markus: Cost question — what's the delta from hosted pay-as-you-go to Dedicated reserved? At our volumes, is Dedicated worth the commit?
[02:10] Samira: Short answer: depends on steady-state qps and sequence length distribution. We'll send a sizing/pricing worksheet but ballpark: for heavy token workloads like 600 tokens avg you'd often see Dedicated win on unit cost beyond a few million tokens/month, and Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower p95 latency. Hosted is fastest time-to-first-call with credits.
[02:28] Ava: We value PLG — could we start on hosted with credits to get to first demo and then transition to Dedicated if the pilot scales?
[02:35] Samira: Yes, that's common. We'll give trial credits for the POC and a quick start guide — time-to-first-token is often minutes if you use our SDK and a simple endpoint.
[02:44] Priya: Are there sample apps or templates for shipping quickly? We have engineers familiar with Python and Node.
[02:49] Lena: We have quickstart templates: Node/Express and Python Flask demos, plus an example that shows batching and prefix caching. We'll link the repo.
[02:58] [00:03:00] Priya: On performance — you mentioned batching and KV caching. How does that affect latency for single-turn requests? I worry batching might add queuing.
[03:11] Diego: Good question. Our runtime supports continuous batching but respects latency SLOs; you can set SLO-based routing and lower batch timeouts for low-latency paths. Also prefix/KV cache avoids re-computing initial tokens. For single-turn sub-300ms p50 with 600 tokens, that'll be tight on some models — we usually recommend model choices and quantization to trade-off cost/latency.
[03:34] Priya: Which models are best for that? We currently look at open models similar to gpt-j/ggml, but we care about inference speed.
[03:41] Diego: We have curated models with performance profiles. For low latency at that token length you'd consider a trimmed instruction-tuned model or a variant with kv-cache friendly chunking. We'll propose a couple: small-medium family and a 7-13B quantized variant.
[03:55] Jonah: For Dedicated and Private, what's the integration path for our KMS? We use AWS KMS and some HSM for key policies.
[04:03] Lena: Dedicated and Private support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys. For Private we can support HSM-backed keys in your network. We'll share our KMS integration guide.
[04:12] Jonah: Good. Also audit logs — can we retain logs in our S3?
[04:16] Samira: Yes, we offer long-term log retention add-ons and can forward audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. We'll include the log ingestion doc.
[04:24] [00:04:50] Markus: On timeline: we want a demo to product stakeholders 2-3 weeks out. Is hosted quickstart realistic?
[04:33] Samira: Absolutely. If you supply 3 prompt sets and a small sample dataset, our SDK integration plus the quickstart templates should get you to first token in under a day, but product-quality demo usually takes a bit more — 1-2 weeks. We'll grant credits to cover that.
[04:46] Priya: What about rate limits on the trial? We need to run a small load test to validate p95 latency.
[04:52] Diego: Trial accounts have default quotas but we can temporarily raise limits for a scheduled benchmark. We typically run a 2-hour benchmark in our hosted sandbox to reproduce your qps profile.
[05:01] Ava: If we go hosted then Dedicated, how does model versioning work — do we have to change calls or is it transparent?
[05:08] Lena: Same API. You pin model versions in the control plane and rollouts are managed; canary and A/B are supported. No code changes if you keep the same model name, just change config.
[05:18] [00:05:40] Markus: Great. Security review — do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO certifications?
[05:24] Samira: Yes SOC2 Type II, and we have ISO27001 in progress (expected later this year). We'll attach the compliance pack.
[05:32] Jonah: For the legal/procurement sequence — what's the lead time on Dedicated capacity provisioning?
[05:37] Diego: Dedicated pools usually take 2-4 weeks to provision depending on region and GPU availability. Private (on-prem) can be 6-12 weeks depending on appliances. That's why many teams prototype on hosted while the dedicated order is in flight.
[05:51] Priya: One concern — we have customers that require data residency in EU. Do you have EU-hosted regions for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:58] Samira: Yes, we have EU regions for both modes. Private can be fully on-prem for strict residency. We'll note region options in the pricing doc.
[06:07] [00:06:40] Markus: For the pilot success criteria — product wants a 2-week pilot with x% accuracy on routing suggestions (we'll provide eval set) and latency targets you heard earlier. Can Redwood help with quality monitoring?
[06:19] Diego: Redwood Optimize includes prompt/quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval sets. We can wire your eval suite to highlight regressions during the pilot.
[06:28] Priya: What's the expected delta in tokenization and token costs for long context? Any tips to reduce cost?
[06:34] Lena: Prefetching, prefix caching, and aggressive context trimming help. Also quantized models reduce compute costs. We can run a tokenization profile for your prompts to estimate token counts and recommend prompt engineering tips.
[06:46] [00:07:20] Jonah: Any third-party dependencies that could leak data? Like if hosted calls go through some shared cache?
[06:28] Diego: All customer requests are logically isolated; hosted uses multi-tenant but we provide strong tenancy isolation for customer data in transit and at rest. For absolute isolation go Dedicated or Private. For hosted we do not use shared KV to persist PII across tenants.
[07:06] Markus: Let's talk numbers — can you walk through an example total cost estimate for 10 qps @ 600 tokens average for a month? Even a roughing will help us decide host vs dedicated.
[07:16] Samira: Sure, very rough: 10 qps * 600 tokens * 60s * 3600*24*30 would be huge if run always. But pilot is smaller — if you run 24/7 that equates to ~15M tokens/day, but pilots typically run subset. We'll produce a worksheet with three scenarios (prototype, pilot, production) with token math and estimated Hosted per-token vs Dedicated per-hour GPU.
[07:38] Priya: For our pilot we expect 10 qps but with 30% of requests being internal tests — so lower. The worksheet will help.
[07:45] [00:08:10] Ava: One practical question — do you have examples that integrate Redwood with our existing stack (Kafka + event ingest)? We want inference to be called from an async pipeline.
[07:56] Lena: Yes, we have patterns for both synchronous API calls and event-driven async invocation. We can show a sample that uses a lightweight fan-out service to call Redwood endpoints and handle responses into your pipelines.
[08:07] Jonah: Any built-in retry/backoff policies? We want graceful degradation and fallback to smaller models.
[08:12] Diego: Yes, our smart routing can fallback to a cheaper model variant or different region on capacity constraints. We also have client-side SDKs with retry/backoff and server-side policies for automatic fallback.
[08:23] [00:08:40] Markus: Competitor check — we've also chatted with Anthropic and OpenAI. Why choose Redwood?
[08:30] Samira: Quick reasons: production-first runtime optimized for inference economics, consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private, and observability — token-level cost and latency breakdown, rollouts, and easy migration path to private. Also our pricing and Dedicated options are designed for predictable unit cost.
[08:47] Priya: For the demo, can we use Redwood's streaming responses for partial output? Our UI shows partial suggestions incrementally.
[08:55] Lena: Streaming is supported, yes — we offer chunked streaming and function/tool calling support for structured outputs.
[09:02] [00:09:20] Samira: I'll recap quickly and then we can call out owners. We will: provide credits for the quickstart, share pricing worksheet and Dedicated sizing template, provide KMS/HSM integration guide, SOC2/compliance pack, quickstart repo links, and schedule a benchmark window for a 2-hour run.
[09:22] Markus: Sounds good. One more from security — what's your incident response posture and do you do penetration tests?
[09:29] Diego: We do regular pen tests and can share summary reports. Our incident response includes customer notifications, and for Dedicated/Private we can do contractual obligations around notifications. We'll include the security contacts in the pack.
[09:42] Priya: Ok, logistics — can we have the pricing and docs this week? We need to align procurement.
[09:49] Samira: We'll target sending the pack and worksheet by Thursday (2026-04-29).
[09:54] Ava: Great, and we'll prepare our prompt sets and sample traffic by next Monday (2026-05-04).
[10:01] Jonah: And I'll send compliance questions by 2026-05-04.
[10:05] [00:10:55] Action recap (quick):
- Samira: pricing worksheet, trial credits, compliance pack (due 2026-04-29)
- Diego: Dedicated sizing + estimate (due 2026-04-29)
- Priya: prompt sets + sample qps profile (due 2026-05-04)
- Jonah: compliance Qs (due 2026-05-04)
- Schedule benchmark week of 2026-05-11 (AE + SE to coordinate)

[00:11:30] Closing remarks:
Samira: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and the docs. Happy to jump into a hands-on pairing session during the benchmark.
Markus: Thanks, looking forward.

[00:11:50] End of call.
notes: Referenced artifacts: Quickstart repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart), Dedicated sizing template (linked in follow-up email), SOC2 summary (doc link), Pricing worksheet (to be attached). Customer emphasized PLG first then Dedicated/Private for compliance-bound customers.
